playlounge.name: Play Lounge
playlounge.description: Multiplayer board game platform for web and mobile

versions.summary: Documents the addition of optional push-to-talk voice chat in private invite-link games. Adds a dedicated Voice Chat section covering availability, opt-in, what is processed, and user controls; corrects two now-inaccurate claims in the do-not-collect list ("Microphone or audio recordings" and "no chat features"); discloses the self-operated LiveKit voice relay; and states that voice is unavailable to children and unavailable in random matchmaking. No other privacy practices changed. Also corrects a pre-existing inaccuracy: the document described Google AdMob and AdSense advertising that the app does not contain. Play Lounge carries no third-party ad SDK and reads no advertising identifier; the only promotions are self-served listings for our own apps.
highlights: New Section 8 "Voice Chat" — availability, opt-in, processing, and controls
Removed inaccurate Google AdMob/AdSense advertising claims — the app has no ad networks
Voice limited to private invite-link games; never offered in random matchmaking
Voice requires a 13+ age confirmation; children cannot enable the microphone
Audio is relayed live and never recorded, stored, transcribed, or listened to
Push-to-talk: the microphone is open only while the talk button is held
LiveKit voice relay (self-operated on Fly.io) disclosed as infrastructure
Google Play Data Safety entry added for audio: collected, not stored
Corrected "no chat features" to "no text chat features"
All other practices unchanged — no accounts, no tracking, no permanent storage

versions.summary: Initial privacy policy. Establishes privacy-first design with no accounts, session-only data, and minimal collection practices.
highlights: No user accounts or personal information required

versions.summary: Adds terms for optional push-to-talk voice chat in private invite-link games. Section 4.3 previously asserted that the Service has no communication features; it is rewritten to describe voice chat and to set conduct rules for it. Also clarifies that voice creates no retained user content (nothing is recorded), notes the 13+ age confirmation, and corrects the children's-use section to say "no text chat". All other terms unchanged. Also corrects a pre-existing inaccuracy: the document described Google AdMob and AdSense advertising that the app does not contain. Play Lounge carries no third-party ad SDK and reads no advertising identifier; the only promotions are self-served listings for our own apps.
highlights: Section 4.3 retitled from "No Communication Features" to "Communication Features"
Removed inaccurate Google AdMob/AdSense advertising claims — the app has no ad networks
Voice conduct rules: no harassment, threats, hateful or explicit content, impersonation, or soliciting personal information
Recording or redistributing the other player's audio without consent is prohibited
Voice limited to private invite-link games; never in random matchmaking
Voice requires a 13+ age confirmation (Section 1.2)
Section 6.3 clarified — voice creates no retained user content
Section 14.1 corrected to "no text chat"; voice unavailable to children
Reporting path for voice misuse: hello@neuera.app
All other terms unchanged

versions.summary: Updated to reflect the rollout of Apple in-app purchases on iOS and additional opt-in flows. Added Apple Inc. as a sub-processor for App Store payment processing, restructured the iOS/Android permissions section to list optional permissions invoked by the Stripe SDK (camera, photo library, biometrics, approximate location) and the new opt-in contact-import flow (iOS Contacts / Android READ_CONTACTS), removed absolute 'does not collect' claims that no longer fit the optional flows, and noted that account deletion is now available in-app at Settings → Delete Account.
highlights: Apple Inc. added as a sub-processor for iOS in-app purchase processing (StoreKit)
Stripe role clarified: Android and web only (cards, Google Pay)
New §2.5 documents opt-in permission flows (contacts, camera, photo library, biometrics, location)
Android READ_CONTACTS added for opt-in 'Import from contacts'
iOS permission section expanded to list all Info.plist declarations
Apple privacy policy added to third-party notices
Account deletion now available in-app (Settings → Delete Account)
Receipt-validation idempotency added to security controls

versions.summary: Aligned with current product. Disclosed Firebase App Check and Crashlytics, clarified manual-only contact entry, added GDPR/UK lawful bases, expanded retention disclosure for financial records, and listed the iOS/Android permissions actually requested.
highlights: Sub-processors expanded: Firebase Auth, Firebase App Check, Firebase Crashlytics, Twilio, Stripe, Fly.io
Apple Pay and Google Pay disclosed as Stripe-routed payment methods
Manually added contacts only — no OS address-book import
GDPR / UK GDPR rights and lawful bases included
iOS and Android permissions explicitly listed; AD_ID confirmed removed
Financial-records retention up to 7 years for tax and anti-fraud
Standard Contractual Clauses for international transfers
No analytics, telemetry, or advertising SDKs

No advertising or third-party marketing
CCPA compliance for California residents
18+ age requirement
Data security with encryption in transit and at rest

versions.summary: Updated to reflect the rollout of Apple in-app purchases on iOS. Rewrote credit-package pricing to show the actual iOS App Store tiers ($2.99 / $12.99 / $29.99 for 209 / 909 / 2,099 credits) instead of a misleading 1:1 USD-to-credits table. Split the refund policy into Stripe (we refund directly) and Apple (refunds go through reportaproblem.apple.com) sections. Added Apple as a payment processor in §5.7 and called out the in-app account-deletion path in §15.1.
highlights: Real iOS credit tiers disclosed — $2.99 / $12.99 / $29.99 → 209 / 909 / 2,099 credits
In-app amount at time of purchase is authoritative; Android/web may differ
Apple App Store added as iOS payment processor in §5.7
New §6.5 documents Apple's refund flow (reportaproblem.apple.com)
Stripe refund window scoped to Stripe-processed purchases only
§15.1 now references in-app deletion (Settings → Delete Account)
Country count tightened to 'approximately 200 destination countries'

versions.summary: Aligned with current product.
